summary: The ENTD.GW strategy [was launched in January 2025 with ten pillars and 55 interventions to 2030](2025-01-29 Guinea-Bissau launches ENTD.GW national digital transformation strategy (ANG)), and Council of Ministers approval is still pending.
developments:
2025-01-29 — the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 [was launched by the prime minister and the minister responsible for digital transformation, with UNDP support: ten pillars, six objectives, 55 interventions and a roadmap to 2030](2025-01-29 Guinea-Bissau launches ENTD.GW national digital transformation strategy (ANG)).

2025-02-04 — a UNU-EGOV and UNDP follow-up meeting [recorded that Council of Ministers approval of the strategy's decree was still pending](2025-02-04 Digital Transformation Project in Guinea-Bissau with UNU-EGOV & UNDP), which is where the base leaves it: nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 records the decree approved, gazetted or brought into force.

The strategy is [the instrument the World Bank-financed WARDIP programme and the UNDP Mais Digit@l grant both implement](2024-01-01 National Strategy for Digital Transformation in Guinea-Bissau (project)), so the financing behind it is moving while the legal instrument is not.

summary: A National Data Governance and Protection Policy decree [was approved in draft by the Council of Ministers in July 2025](2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)) and has not moved since.
developments:
2025-07-10 — the Council of Ministers [approved the draft decree on a national data governance and protection policy, alongside decrees on interoperability and a national cybersecurity strategy](2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)). Nothing on the base confirms gazettal or entry into force, and nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 touches it.

Of the three decrees approved that day, only the interoperability instrument has moved since, and it moved through a programme announcement rather than a gazette. No data classification standard, no public-sector data catalogue and no data-sharing agreement appears anywhere on this ledger.

summary: A national interoperability regulation for public and private digital systems [was approved by the government in August 2026](2026-08-08-guineabissau-national-interoperability-framework), with no decree number or in-force date named.
developments:
2026-08-08 — the WARDIP programme [announced government approval of a national interoperability framework regulating how public and private digital systems and platforms connect](2026-08-08-guineabissau-national-interoperability-framework), presented as Guinea-Bissau's contribution to the regional programme.

It is the one instrument of the three [draft decrees the Council of Ministers approved on 10 July 2025](2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)) that has moved since. What the record does not carry is the instrument itself: no decree number, no gazettal and no entry-into-force date, and the approval is reported by the World Bank-backed programme that supports the work rather than by an official journal.

No data exchange platform appears on this ledger for the regulation to govern.

summary: A National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency [was committed to in January 2025](2025-01-22 Guinea-Bissau presents cybersecurity study, plans National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency); nothing on the base confirms it exists.
developments:
2025-01-22 — the government presented the results of a WARDIP cybersecurity feasibility study and [committed to creating a National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency](2025-01-22 Guinea-Bissau presents cybersecurity study, plans National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency), framed by the minister responsible as central to data protection and digital sovereignty.

The commitment predates the window and no source since confirms the agency established, staffed or operational. The country therefore has no supervisory authority on the record, and the [draft data governance and protection decree approved in July 2025](2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)) is not confirmed in force either, so neither the body nor the instrument it would enforce is in place.

summary: Readiness rests on [a draft policy decree](2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)) and [an agency still only committed to](2025-01-22 Guinea-Bissau presents cybersecurity study, plans National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency), with no enacted statute behind either.
developments:
The base holds no data protection statute for Guinea-Bissau. What it holds instead is a policy [decree approved in draft on 10 July 2025](2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)) and not confirmed in force, and an agency [committed to in January 2025](2025-01-22 Guinea-Bissau presents cybersecurity study, plans National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency) and not confirmed established.

Neither moved in the twelve months to 2026-08-26. No registration or notification regime, no data subject rights case, no enforcement action and no cross-border transfer rule appears on the ledger.

The biometric identity network, the civil registry digitisation and the electoral register update reported elsewhere in this report are all proceeding without any of it, which is what the absence costs.

summary: Guinea-Bissau [joined AUDA-NEPAD's programme for African developing island economies in July 2026](2026-07-24-auda-nepad-island-economies-programme-launch), whose roadmap to 2031 includes digital transformation.
developments:
2026-07-24 — at the ministerial segment in Abidjan, AUDA-NEPAD [launched a Programme for African Developing Island Economies covering Guinea-Bissau among seven states, with ministers adopting a communique committing to a 2026-2031 roadmap on six pillars including digital transformation](2026-07-24-auda-nepad-island-economies-programme-launch).

It is a continental commitment rather than a national action, and no country-level implementation under it is reported. The country's substantive regional work sits elsewhere on this ledger — the ECOWAS biometric credential and the World Bank's West Africa regional digital programme — and neither is an AUDA-NEPAD instrument.

No ECOWAS or UEMOA policy instrument adopted domestically appears in the window.

summary: The ECOWAS biometric identity card [reached its first reported field issuance](2026-03-16 Women traders receive ECOWAS biometric ID in Sao Domingos, Guinea-Bissau), 262 cards to women cross-border traders in Sao Domingos.
developments:
2026-03-16 — the National Borders Commission [issued 262 ECOWAS biometric identity cards to women cross-border traders in Sao Domingos, Cacheu](2026-03-16 Women traders receive ECOWAS biometric ID in Sao Domingos, Guinea-Bissau), under a Guinea-Bissau-Senegal mobility project backed by ECOWAS and financed by GIZ. It is the first field distribution the base records.

The standing position is that Guinea-Bissau is [one of six ECOWAS states to have fully operationalised the credential](2025-06-10 Guinea-Bissau deploys efforts to digitize birth registration, national ID systems), so what moved in the window is use rather than adoption.

The only other shared regional asset on the ledger is the ACE submarine cable, reported under international bandwidth. No regional data centre, internet exchange point or interconnection arrangement appears.

progress: Regressed, a new online-falsehoods offence with enforcement left unstated
summary: The transitional parliament [passed a law on the dissemination of false information online](2026-05-23 Guinea-Bissau CNT passes Digital Integrity (online falsehoods) Law), and the government [first invoked it in July 2026](2026-07-21-ang-ministerio-comunicacao-tiktok-desmentido).
developments:
2026-05-23 — the transitional parliament [passed unanimously, with amendments, a Digital Integrity law on the dissemination of false information on the internet](2026-05-23 Guinea-Bissau CNT passes Digital Integrity (online falsehoods) Law), presented by the government spokesman as aimed at those who spread hate and act against the State. The publication date, the entry-into-force date and the enforcement mechanism — including how it would reach citizens abroad — are not stated in the record.

2026-07-21 — the Ministry of Communication [invoked the law for the first time the base records, in denying a claim that TikTok was to be shut down](2026-07-21-ang-ministerio-comunicacao-tiktok-desmentido).

It is the only instrument on this ledger addressing online speech, and nothing records a court, a regulator or a civil-society challenge testing it. No consultation on the bill appears either.

summary: A MIGA guarantee [covers Sonatel's equity investment in Orange Bissau](2025-01-01-miga-gnb-orange-bissau-2025-orange-bissau-sa-telecoms-operator-guarantee) at US$25.4m, and no new private commitment appears in the window.
developments:
The standing position is a [US$25,435,357 MIGA guarantee to Sonatel SA covering its equity investment in Orange Bissau S.A.](2025-01-01-miga-gnb-orange-bissau-2025-orange-bissau-sa-telecoms-operator-guarantee), approved for the 2025 financial year as part of a combined Orange Guinea and Guinea-Bissau programme, with nothing disbursed as captured.

Nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 records a disbursement, a new guarantee or a second private transaction. The one other private commitment on the ledger is the operator-backed training programme reported under digital literacy, which states no financial value.

The fibre backbone the country's connectivity depends on is to be built by a private wholesale operator under exclusive licence, and that operator has not been selected — so the largest private commitment in prospect is not yet a transaction.

summary: A [World Bank WARDIP grant](2023-11-07-worldbank-dtfa-wardip-sop1-pad4756) and a [UNDP digital transformation programme](2025-01-01-undp-gnb-mais-digital-2025-mais-digitl-for-guinea-bissau) are the standing development-partner financing, neither reporting new movement in the window.
developments:
Two commitments stand. The World Bank's [Guinea-Bissau allocation under the regional WARDIP programme is US$60.00m in IDA grant plus US$0.50m of government counterpart](2023-11-07-worldbank-dtfa-wardip-sop1-pad4756), [launched in country in April 2025](2025-04-02 President Embalo launches WARDIP in Guinea-Bissau) and [carried in the Bank's own project record](2023-01-01-world-bank-gnb-2023-wardip-sop1-guinea-bissau-bw01). UNDP's Mais Digit@l programme [committed US$3,360,500 to implement the national digital transformation strategy, of which US$566,152 is recorded disbursed](2025-01-01-undp-gnb-mais-digital-2025-mais-digitl-for-guinea-bissau).

No fresher disbursement figure, extension or successor appears in the twelve months to 2026-08-26, and no third development partner appears on the ledger. What this money moved is reported elsewhere: the backbone design and its safeguards study, and the interoperability regulation.

summary: Internet use was [last measured at 32.5% penetration, 723,000 users, with two-thirds of the population offline](2025-03-03 Digital 2025 - Guinea-Bissau (DataReportal)), before the window opened.
developments:
2025-03-03 — the last measurement the base holds [puts internet users at 723,000 and penetration at 32.5%, leaving 67.5% of the population offline](2025-03-03 Digital 2025 - Guinea-Bissau (DataReportal)).

The figure predates the twelve-month window and nothing fresher was published into it: no regulator return, no operator disclosure and no household survey covering internet use appears for Guinea-Bissau. The census reported under Censuses and surveys is the one national data collection inside the window, and its preliminary release carries no connectivity variable.

So the direction of internet use over the window is unmeasured, at the point where the national backbone is still in design and satellite is the only service to have entered the market.

summary: The WARDIP-GB backbone [reached its environmental and social safeguards study in May 2026](2026-05-21 WARDIP-GB fibre backbone environmental and social impact study (EIASS)), on a [2,877 km, 56-node design](2026-01-01 Guinea-Bissau National Fibre-Optic Backbone specifications (WARDIP-GB)) not yet built.
developments:
The country has no national fibre backbone. The design for one [specifies 2,877 km over 56 nodes in four phases, targeting coverage of more than 99% of the population and operation by a private wholesale operator under exclusive licence](2026-01-01 Guinea-Bissau National Fibre-Optic Backbone specifications (WARDIP-GB)); that specification is itself undated and carried at year precision.

2026-05-21 — the [environmental and social impact study was published](2026-05-21 WARDIP-GB fibre backbone environmental and social impact study (EIASS)), which is the movement in the window: the project passes from design toward implementation procurement.

The starting position was thinner. In [August 2025 the country was seeking deployment experience from Chad with no fixed design published](2025-08-29 Fibre-optic deployment - Guinea-Bissau wants to learn from Chad), after [the programme's launch in April 2025](2025-04-02 President Embalo launches WARDIP in Guinea-Bissau). No construction contract, no selected wholesale operator and no built phase appears on the ledger.

progress: No change, a second cable approved at feasibility but not built
summary: The ACE submarine cable [remains the country's only international fibre link](2025-08-29 Fibre-optic deployment - Guinea-Bissau wants to learn from Chad), with a second, ECOWAS-led cable [approved at feasibility stage in October 2025](2025-10-22-ecowas-segundo-cabo-submarino-validacao-estudo-cabo-verde).
developments:
International capacity rests on a single submarine cable. The ACE landing [is the country's first and only international fibre-optic connection, live since March 2023](2025-08-29 Fibre-optic deployment - Guinea-Bissau wants to learn from Chad), and it is held only as background in a secondary record: no primary on the landing itself is on the base.

2025-10-22 - member-state experts with their technical and financial partners [reviewed and approved the feasibility study for a second submarine cable serving Cabo Verde, Liberia, Sierra Leone and Guinea-Bissau](2025-10-22-ecowas-segundo-cabo-submarino-validacao-estudo-cabo-verde), at a workshop the ECOWAS Project Preparation and Development Unit convened in Monrovia.

That cable is at feasibility and nothing further: no route, cost, landing site or construction date is published. Nor does any capacity, price or utilisation figure for the existing link appear on the ledger, so the base can state what carries the traffic and not how much it carries.

The national backbone that would distribute that capacity inland is still in design.

summary: Starlink [has been commercially live since June 2025](2025-06-19 Starlink enters Guinea-Bissau) under [a provisional authorisation from the regulator](2025-04-10 ARN-TIC grants Starlink Guinea-Bissau provisional authorization), and nothing moved in the window.
developments:
2025-06-19 — Starlink [entered service, Guinea-Bissau's seventh West African and twentieth continental market](2025-06-19 Starlink enters Guinea-Bissau), following [a provisional authorisation from ARN-TIC in April 2025](2025-04-10 ARN-TIC grants Starlink Guinea-Bissau provisional authorization). Both events fall before the twelve-month window.

Nothing since records a definitive licence, a second satellite operator, a subscriber figure or a tariff, so what the base holds is the fact of availability and nothing about its reach. An initial provisional licence referred to in the launch record is not itself held.

Satellite is the only service reaching what the absent national backbone does not, which is what makes the missing uptake figure matter.

summary: A national cybersecurity strategy [sits in a draft decree](2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)) and the agency to run it [is still only committed to](2025-01-22 Guinea-Bissau presents cybersecurity study, plans National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency).
developments:
2025-01-22 — the government [presented the results of a WARDIP cybersecurity feasibility study and committed to a National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency](2025-01-22 Guinea-Bissau presents cybersecurity study, plans National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency).

2025-07-10 — the Council of Ministers [approved the draft decree for a national cybersecurity strategy](2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)). Neither instrument is confirmed gazetted or in force, and both predate the twelve-month window.

Nothing in the window moved either. No computer emergency response team, no cybercrime prosecution, no reported incident and no critical-infrastructure designation appears on this ledger, so readiness is a study, a draft strategy and a promised agency, with no operational capability recorded behind them.

summary: A [third production centre in Biombo took the national network to 18](2026-02-11 Semlex Guinea-Bissau strengthens access to biometric identification), and the ECOWAS credential [reached first field issuance](2026-03-16 Women traders receive ECOWAS biometric ID in Sao Domingos, Guinea-Bissau).
developments:
2026-02-11 — the contractor Semlex [opened a production centre at Safim in Biombo, its third in that region and rated at 100 cards a day, bringing the national network to 18 biometric identity production centres, with further centres planned for Sao Domingos and Bolama](2026-02-11 Semlex Guinea-Bissau strengthens access to biometric identification).

2026-03-16 — the ECOWAS biometric card [was issued in the field for the first time the base records, 262 cards to women cross-border traders in Sao Domingos](2026-03-16 Women traders receive ECOWAS biometric ID in Sao Domingos, Guinea-Bissau).

Beneath both is a standing position of [a functional biometric national identity card system, with Guinea-Bissau one of six ECOWAS states to have fully operationalised the regional credential](2025-06-10 Guinea-Bissau deploys efforts to digitize birth registration, national ID systems). What the ledger does not hold is an enrolment total, a coverage rate, an authentication service or any legal instrument governing the system: the movement is in production capacity, not in what the credential does.

progress: Advanced, on the regional regulator's 2024 figures
summary: Active electronic-money accounts [grew 33.28% in 2024, the union's second-fastest rate](2026-01-01-bceao-services-financiers-numeriques-uemoa-2024), on a regional report published in January 2026.
developments:
2026-01-01 — the regional central bank's annual report on digital financial services [records Guinea-Bissau's active electronic-money accounts up 33.28% in 2024, the union's second-highest growth rate after Togo, on a 1.94% share of accounts opened union-wide and about 1% of regional transaction value, served by two electronic-money issuing initiatives of the 69 operating across the union](2026-01-01-bceao-services-financiers-numeriques-uemoa-2024).

The data year is 2024 and the publication falls inside the window, so what the window holds is the arrival of the figure rather than the growth itself. These are shares within a regional report and not a national release: the base holds no account total, no transaction count and no payments statistic published in Guinea-Bissau.

No named mobile-money service, no interoperable switch and no consumer-protection rule for payments appears anywhere on this ledger.

summary: Birth registration [stands at about 46% of under-fives](2025-06-10 Guinea-Bissau deploys efforts to digitize birth registration, national ID systems), with [SIREC digitising births, deaths and marriages](2025-06-01 Guinea-Bissau to digitize civil identification, registry and notary services) and no fresher figure since.
developments:
The Ministry of Justice's civil registration office [describes SIREC digitising births, deaths and marriages with UNDP-trained officers, roughly three months into a Bissau-first rollout, against a target of at least 90% registration, with registration of under-fives at about 46% from an undated 23.4% baseline](2025-06-10 Guinea-Bissau deploys efforts to digitize birth registration, national ID systems). A parallel account [covers the digitisation of civil identification, registry and notary services](2025-06-01 Guinea-Bissau to digitize civil identification, registry and notary services).

Behind them, a UNDP project co-financed by Switzerland [built a digitisation centre and software to recover the paper civil-registry books](2024-01-01 Building a National Identification System - Scanning and Digitizing the Civil Registry Books in Guinea-Bissau), held at year precision.

All of it predates the twelve-month window. No dated confirmation of regional extension, no fresher registration rate and no death or marriage registration figure appears in it.

summary: The updated electoral register [was handed to the elections commission on 18 August 2026 recording 966,152 voters](2026-08-18-guinea-bissau-gtape-entrega-cadernos-eleitorais-cne), unchanged in size from the last update.
developments:
2026-08-18 — the electoral register [was handed to the elections commission in both physical and electronic form ahead of the 30 August referendum, recording 966,152 registered voters](2026-08-18-guinea-bissau-gtape-entrega-cadernos-eleitorais-cne).

2026-08-17 — the operation behind it [issued 25,146 replacement voter cards over thirty days from 13 July, worked by 51 brigades covering every region](2026-08-17-guineabissau-gtape-25146-voter-card-second-copies).

The electorate total is unchanged from the previous update, so the operation replaced cards rather than added registrants. No audit, no de-duplication statement and no link between the register and the biometric identity system is published. It is the only register on this ledger that moved in the window.

summary: A government and operator programme [stood up its coordination committee in May 2026](2026-05-07 Telecel and Guinea-Bissau Government launch STARTOCODE Coordination Committee), to train 1,000 young people a year for four years.
developments:
2026-05-07 — a joint decree [created the STARTOCODE coordination and monitoring committee, formalising a programme to train 1,000 young people a year over four years in programming, data analysis and cloud computing, with a stated emphasis on women and people with disabilities](2026-05-07 Telecel and Guinea-Bissau Government launch STARTOCODE Coordination Committee). The record is the operator's own announcement.

It is the only digital skills programme on this ledger and the only training commitment of any kind. No enrolment figure, no first cohort and no completion is reported, so what exists is the governance structure rather than evidence of training delivered.

No measurement of digital literacy in the population appears anywhere on the base for Guinea-Bissau.

summary: The fourth census [released preliminary results in July 2026 putting the population at 2,191,202](2026-07-23-ang-rgph4-resultados-preliminares-ine), in [the country's first fully digital count](2026-07-23-guinea-bissau-rgph4-first-fully-digital-census-preliminary-results).
developments:
2026-07-23 — the national statistics institute [released preliminary results of the fourth General Population and Housing Census: a population of 2,191,202, 50.7% women and 45.7% urban, across 304,939 households and 559,303 dwellings](2026-07-23-ang-rgph4-resultados-preliminares-ine), against 1,449,230 at the 2009 count.

It is [the country's first fully digital census, collected by computer-assisted personal interview and leaving a digital cartography and technology base for future operations](2026-07-23-guinea-bissau-rgph4-first-fully-digital-census-preliminary-results), with UNFPA as lead technical agency and [World Bank support for the statistical capacity behind it](2026-07-24-ang-rgph4-banco-mundial-capacidade-estatistica).

Full tabulations are pending. One record's headline population differs from its own body and from the other two, and the base resolves it against them. No statistics law, no national strategy for the development of statistics and no other survey appears on this ledger.

summary: The [US$60m regional digital programme launched nationally](2026-08-01-gnb-ang-wardip-lancamento-nacional-digitalizacao) in August 2026, giving the 2025-2030 strategy a delivery vehicle.
developments:
The national digital transformation strategy for 2025-2030 sits on the ledger as enacted and approved. What it lacked was money and a programme.

Both arrived: the [programme launched nationally in August 2026 covering connectivity, data protection, the digital economy and electronic government](2026-08-01-gnb-ang-wardip-lancamento-nacional-digitalizacao), described by the minister as a pillar of effective public services, with a [procurement plan and implementation reporting behind it](2026-03-17-worldbank-wardip-p176932-procurement-plan-guinea-bissau).

summary: A [2026-2031 strategic plan for the universal access fund](2026-05-01-wardip-plano-estrategico-fundo-acesso-servicos-universais-2026-2031) sets targets for closing the coverage gap.
developments:
A [legal review recommended restructuring the universal access fund](2025-10-30-guinebissau-wardip-revisao-quadro-legal-acesso-servico-universal) in October 2025, which is the base's judgement on the instrument as it stood.

The [2026-2031 roadmap and financing plan](2025-11-24-arn-guine-bissau-plano-estrategico-fasu-2026-2031) followed in November and was [delivered to the regulator in May 2026](2026-05-01-wardip-plano-estrategico-fundo-acesso-servicos-universais-2026-2031). It is a fund plan rather than a broadband strategy, and it is the nearest thing the country holds to one.

summary: A [feasibility study scoped a national cloud](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity) alongside a security operations centre and an incident response team.
developments:
The [study of September 2025](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity) is the only document in the base that treats where Guinean government data should sit: it scopes a national cloud, a security operations centre, a national incident response team and a draft cybersecurity strategy.

A data centre appears separately as a budget line: the [2026 budget carries a named digital transformation investment line covering the financial system, a data centre, communications and an enterprise system](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026).

summary: [Decree 27/2025](2025-10-31-gnb-decreto-27-2025-regulamento-nacional-interoperabilidade) sets national interoperability rules and [consultants delivered the platform design](2025-11-15-wardip-gnb-publication-page-devemerge-interoperability-deliverable) in November 2025.
developments:
The framework moved from intention to instrument in the window. The government [approved the national interoperability regulation by decree in October 2025](2025-10-31-gnb-decreto-27-2025-regulamento-nacional-interoperabilidade), with the gazette date disputed in the record.

Consultants then [delivered the interoperability structure, the platform and an action plan for digitising the main public services](2025-11-15-wardip-gnb-publication-page-devemerge-interoperability-deliverable). The cabinet had [approved the data governance and protection policy, the cybersecurity strategy and system interoperability together in September 2025](2025-09-25-ang-conselho-ministros-politica-governanca-protecao-dados).

summary: No artificial intelligence strategy exists; the subject reaches policy only through [misinformation cooperation](2026-06-24-voicegambia-gambia-guinea-bissau-cooperation-misinformation-ai) and a [regional framework](2026-07-01-ang-quadro-politico-integridade-informacao-africa-ocidental-sahel).
developments:
Nothing in the base records a Guinean artificial intelligence strategy, policy or working group.

Where the subject appears it appears as risk: [specialists debated artificial intelligence, ethics and disinformation at a Bissau forum](2025-11-11-nokunsi-djumbai-inteligencia-artificial-bissau) in November 2025; [ministers of Guinea-Bissau and The Gambia pledged joint action as artificial intelligence accelerates the spread of unverified information](2026-06-24-voicegambia-gambia-guinea-bissau-cooperation-misinformation-ai) in June 2026; and a [regional framework adopted the same month commits fifteen West African states to information-integrity laws](2026-07-01-ang-quadro-politico-integridade-informacao-africa-ocidental-sahel).

summary: No localisation rule exists; the only hosting question on the record is the [national cloud the feasibility study scopes](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity).
developments:
The [data governance and protection policy approved by cabinet in September 2025](2025-09-25-ang-conselho-ministros-politica-governanca-protecao-dados) is the instrument that would carry a localisation rule, and nothing in the base records one inside it.

What is being planned is capacity rather than restriction: the [feasibility study scopes a national cloud](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity) and the [2026 budget names a data centre](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026). Neither says what must be held in it.

summary: No open data policy exists; the [access to information bill](2024-10-01-unesco-guine-bissau-validation-projet-loi-acces-information) remains in development and no portal is on the record.
developments:
The base holds no Guinean open data policy, licence or portal.

The adjacent instrument is the access to information bill the ledger carries as in development. Publication that does happen is done by institutions for their own purposes: the [state budget volume](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026) and the fund's [national summary data page](2024-07-08-imf-pr24262-guinea-bissau-implements-egdds-national-summary-data-page) are the base's only routine releases.

summary: The transitional council [ratified the African Union, Budapest and United Nations conventions](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais) in May 2026.
developments:
Domestic protection has rested on the [regional supplementary act on personal data protection](2010-02-16-ecowas-supplementary-act-personal-data-protection-complete-text) since 2010, with the national policy still in development.

The window's movement is treaty ratification rather than a statute: the [transitional national council ratified the African Union, Budapest and United Nations conventions in May 2026](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais), having [signed the United Nations convention at Hanoi in October 2025](2025-10-25-pj-guine-bissau-adesao-convencao-onu-cibercriminalidade). No domestic data protection act has been passed.

summary: Three cybercrime conventions were [ratified in May 2026](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais) alongside a law against false online information.
developments:
Guinea-Bissau [signed the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime at Hanoi in October 2025](2025-10-25-pj-guine-bissau-adesao-convencao-onu-cibercriminalidade), and the [transitional council ratified it with the African Union and Budapest conventions in May 2026](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais).

The same sitting passed a law against the dissemination of false information online, which the ledger carries as its own row. The institutional side is still scoped rather than built: the [feasibility study proposes a security operations centre and a national incident response team](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity).

summary: No identity statute is held; enrolment runs on a [contracted production network](2026-06-08-gnb-ang-bolama-centro-producao-bilhete-identidade) and the regional card scheme.
developments:
The base holds no Guinean law governing the identity register or the biometric card. What it holds is delivery: an [eighteenth identity card production centre opened in June 2026](2026-06-08-gnb-ang-bolama-centro-producao-bilhete-identidade) and a [third regional enrolment centre in February](2026-03-09-semlex-inauguration-centre-enrolement-sao-domingos).

The governing frame is regional rather than national: [a consultation opened in February 2026 on a roadmap from national identification systems to the regional biometric card](2026-02-09-ecowas-roadmap-foundational-id-to-enbic-consultation).

summary: Payment law is regional: the [central bank's register](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau) licenses six banks, one payment institution and one electronic money issuer.
developments:
No domestic payments statute appears in the base. Authorisation runs through the monetary union: the [first licensed payment institution in the country appeared on the register in September 2025](2025-09-15-bceao-liste-etablissements-paiement-agrees-umoa), and the [June 2026 register carries six banks, one payment institution and one electronic money issuer](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau).

Domestic instruments are administrative rather than legislative: the revenue directorate's [order making the payment platform the sole channel for the tax identification number](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu).

summary: No artificial intelligence instrument exists; the nearest is the [law against false online information](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais) of May 2026.
developments:
The [law passed with amendments in May 2026](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais) addresses false information on social networks and names no technology.

It was passed by a transitional council seated after a takeover whose leaders had [ordered radio shutdowns and blocked four major platforms nationwide](2025-11-27-mfwa-guinea-bissau-military-takeover-media-suspension) in November 2025, which is the context any reading of it has to carry.

summary: The electronic transactions bill remains in development; the regional layer moved instead, with a [paperless customs directive presented at Bissau](2026-04-28-ang-uemoa-bissau-workshop-plataforma-eletronica-documentos-comerciais).
developments:
The electronic transactions bill sits on the ledger as in development and no enacted commerce statute is held.

The movement is regional and sectoral: a [Bissau workshop in April 2026 presented the union's paperless customs directive and a planned trade-document exchange platform](2026-04-28-ang-uemoa-bissau-workshop-plataforma-eletronica-documentos-comerciais). Domestic electronic dealing is happening under tax administration rules rather than commerce law, through the [platform-only value added tax declaration for customs clearance](2025-12-10-dgci-circular-iva-desalfandegamento-kontaktu).

summary: The [2007 framework law](2007-09-10-ine-guine-bissau-lei-6-2007-sistema-estatistico-nacional) still governs, and the census rests on it.
developments:
The national statistical system framework law of 2007 is the governing statute and no amendment appears in the base.

The system it governs is delivering: the [fourth census launched field enumeration in June 2026, the country's first fully digital count since 2009](2026-06-01-unfpa-guinea-bissau-rgph4-census-field-launch), after the institute [opened recruitment for about 5,000 census staff](2025-09-02-ang-ine-gb-plataforma-recrutamento-rgph4) in September 2025.

summary: The access to information bill remains in development, against [platform blocking](2025-11-27-mfwa-guinea-bissau-military-takeover-media-suspension) in November 2025.
developments:
The bill sits on the ledger as in development and nothing in the window records it enacted.

What did move went the other way: after the November 2025 takeover [coup leaders ordered radio shutdowns and blocked Facebook, YouTube, TikTok and Instagram nationwide](2025-11-27-mfwa-guinea-bissau-military-takeover-media-suspension), and the transitional council [passed a law against false online information](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais) six months later.

summary: Eight states [approved a draft land registration harmonisation directive](2026-06-26-uemoa-directive-immatriculation-propriete-fonciere) in June 2026.
developments:
Two harmonisation instruments moved in the window. Eight member states [approved a draft directive harmonising land registration and titling rules across the union](2026-06-26-uemoa-directive-immatriculation-propriete-fonciere) in June 2026, and a [Bissau workshop presented the union's paperless customs directive and a trade-document platform](2026-04-28-ang-uemoa-bissau-workshop-plataforma-eletronica-documentos-comerciais) in April.

On identity, a [regional consultation opened on a roadmap from national identification systems to the common biometric card](2026-02-09-ecowas-roadmap-foundational-id-to-enbic-consultation). No domestic transposition of any of the three is recorded.

summary: Guinea-Bissau [became the first member state to sign the international police privileges agreement](2025-09-12-interpol-president-guinea-bissau-declaration-of-intent) and confirmed regional police data participation.
developments:
The [signature of September 2025](2025-09-12-interpol-president-guinea-bissau-declaration-of-intent) is the base's clearest instrument on cross-border data: a privileges and immunities agreement with the international police organisation, and confirmed participation in the West African police information system.

The protective side is treaty-based rather than domestic: the [three cybercrime conventions ratified in May 2026](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais) and the regional supplementary act on personal data protection.

summary: [Decree 27/2025](2025-10-31-gnb-decreto-27-2025-regulamento-nacional-interoperabilidade) sets national interoperability rules and the [platform design was delivered](2025-11-15-wardip-gnb-publication-page-devemerge-interoperability-deliverable) in November 2025.
developments:
The rule and the design arrived within a month of each other: the government [approved the national interoperability regulation by decree in October 2025](2025-10-31-gnb-decreto-27-2025-regulamento-nacional-interoperabilidade), and consultants [delivered the interoperability structure, the platform and a digitisation action plan for the main public services](2025-11-15-wardip-gnb-publication-page-devemerge-interoperability-deliverable) in November.

What is not yet on the record is any system exchanging data through it. The interoperability platform on the ledger remains in development.

summary: The minister [signalled a plan for a national quality and metrology institute](2025-10-02-jornal-no-pintcha-governo-anuncia-instituto-nacional-qualidade-metrologia) in October 2025.
developments:
Guinea-Bissau has no national standards body in the base. The [announcement of October 2025](2025-10-02-jornal-no-pintcha-governo-anuncia-instituto-nacional-qualidade-metrologia) is a ministerial signal of intent to create a quality and metrology institute, with no statute, budget or premises attached.

Until one exists, standards reach the country through adoption rather than issuance — as with the [common alerting protocol operationalised in May 2026](2026-05-07-inm-gb-operacionalizacao-do-cap-sistemas-de-alerta).

summary: The meteorological institute [operationalised the common alerting protocol](2026-05-07-inm-gb-operacionalizacao-do-cap-sistemas-de-alerta), putting national alerts on search and mapping services.
developments:
The [operationalisation of May 2026](2026-05-07-inm-gb-operacionalizacao-do-cap-sistemas-de-alerta) is the country's clearest adoption of an international data standard: the common alerting protocol, which is what makes a national weather warning appear inside general search and mapping services.

The other adoptions are financial and regional rather than technical: the [payment institution licensing regime of the monetary union](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau) and the [regional biometric card specification](2026-02-09-ecowas-roadmap-foundational-id-to-enbic-consultation).

summary: Platform blocking followed the [November 2025 takeover](2025-11-27-mfwa-guinea-bissau-military-takeover-media-suspension); a [law against false online information](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais) followed in May.
developments:
The channel non-state actors had been using is documented: a [preprint maps online networks of around 445,000 followers driving political mobilisation since 2013](2025-09-10-guinebissau-scielo-preprint-ciberativismo-resistencia).

It narrowed sharply. [Coup leaders ordered radio shutdowns and blocked four major platforms nationwide](2025-11-27-mfwa-guinea-bissau-military-takeover-media-suspension) in November 2025, and the transitional council [passed a law against false online information in May 2026](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais). Structured participation continues in donor programmes — a [youth dialogue closing with policy recommendations](2025-10-01-guinebissau-un-dialogo-com-a-juventude) in October 2025.

summary: The [2026 budget](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026) carries a named digital transformation investment line, inside a CFA 83.2bn investment programme.
developments:
The [budget volume](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026) names a digital transformation line in the public investment programme covering the financial system, a data centre, communications and an enterprise system — the first identified digital allocation the base holds for Guinea-Bissau.

The frame around it is tight: [CFA 530.7bn in revenue and spending, a CFA 79.8bn deficit and a CFA 83.2bn investment programme](2025-12-30-ang-conselho-de-ministros-aprova-oge-2026-guine-bissau). Revenue reform is the fund programme's own condition, with the [payment platform and a taxpayer census named among reform actions](2026-06-01-imf-cr-26-140-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review).

summary: The [eleventh review](2026-06-12-imf-pr-26-204-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review) disbursed a further US$1.6m to US$1.7m, citing revenue administration digitalisation.
developments:
The credit facility is the relationship that sets the reform agenda. The [ninth and tenth reviews disbursed US$3.2m and extended the arrangement to December 2026](2026-03-09-imf-guinea-bissau-country-report-26-83-ninth-tenth-ecf-reviews), and the [eleventh completed in June 2026 disbursing a further US$1.6m to US$1.7m](2026-06-12-imf-pr-26-204-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review).

What it asks for is digital: the [review confirms the revenue administration platform and a taxpayer census as reform actions](2026-06-01-imf-cr-26-140-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review). The digital programme itself is separate and larger, [launched nationally at US$60m in August 2026](2026-08-01-gnb-ang-wardip-lancamento-nacional-digitalizacao).

summary: No new penetration series was published; the ledger's own measures remain the base's figures.
developments:
Nothing in this batch updates the mobile or internet penetration measures the ledger already carries.

What moved instead is supply and enforcement: the [national fibre backbone tender was relaunched in March 2026 after two cancelled rounds](2026-03-17-wardip-concurso-internacional-rede-nacional-fibra-optica), and the regulator [warned that only the licensed satellite operator may sell its service, with illegal resale to face sanctions](2025-09-25-arn-guine-bissau-comunicado-fornecimento-ilegal-internet-starlink).

summary: No tariff or affordability figure is published; the [universal access fund plan](2026-05-01-wardip-plano-estrategico-fundo-acesso-servicos-universais-2026-2031) is the instrument aimed at the gap.
developments:
The base holds no Guinean retail tariff, price basket or affordability ratio.

The instrument that would address affordability is the universal access fund, which a [legal review recommended restructuring](2025-10-30-guinebissau-wardip-revisao-quadro-legal-acesso-servico-universal) in October 2025 and for which a [2026-2031 strategic and financing plan](2026-05-01-wardip-plano-estrategico-fundo-acesso-servicos-universais-2026-2031) was delivered in May 2026. Neither publishes a price target.

summary: No exchange point is recorded; the [national fibre backbone](2026-03-17-wardip-concurso-internacional-rede-nacional-fibra-optica) it would sit on is still at tender.
developments:
Nothing in the base records an internet exchange point in Guinea-Bissau, operating or planned.

The domestic network that would justify one is not built: the [national fibre backbone tender was relaunched in March 2026 after two prior rounds were cancelled](2026-03-17-wardip-concurso-internacional-rede-nacional-fibra-optica), and the [procurement plan records that history](2026-03-17-worldbank-wardip-p176932-procurement-plan-guinea-bissau).

summary: A data centre appears as a [named line in the 2026 budget](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026); no facility or capacity figure is published.
developments:
No Guinean data centre capacity figure exists in the base, from any provider.

What exists is intention with money attached: the [2026 budget's digital transformation line covers a data centre alongside the financial system, communications and an enterprise system](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026), and the [cybersecurity feasibility study scopes a national cloud](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity).

summary: The state's own hosting is a [budget line and a scoped national cloud](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity), not a facility.
developments:
The [feasibility study of September 2025](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity) scopes a national cloud along with a security operations centre and an incident response team; nothing has been built.

The [2026 budget names a data centre inside the digital transformation investment line](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026). Neither source gives a location, a capacity or a delivery date.

summary: No backup arrangement is described anywhere in the base for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base states where any Guinean government system's data is copied to, or whether it is.

The documents that would say so are forward-looking: the [national cloud scoped in the feasibility study](2025-09-18-cybil-feasibility-study-guinea-bissau-cybersecurity) and the [data centre named in the 2026 budget](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026). Neither mentions redundancy or a second site.

summary: The only powered facility on the record is a [US$5m solar-powered medical warehouse](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund).
developments:
No Guinean data centre exists to have a power provision, so the base's only evidence on powering digital infrastructure is a logistics building: a [US$5m solar-powered warehouse giving the central procurement body real-time medicine tracking](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund).

Solar is the pattern where reliability matters, and it is donor-financed in both recorded cases.

summary: No grid reliability figure is published; digital facilities are [solar-powered where reliability matters](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund).
developments:
The base holds no generation, outage or access figure for the Guinean grid.

What it holds is the workaround: the [medical warehouse commissioned in October 2025 is solar-powered](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund), and the [offline learning platform installed for justice-sector training](2026-07-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-apr-jun-2026-digital-skills-justice) is designed to work without a connection. Both are designed around infrastructure that cannot be relied on.

summary: No rural electrification figure or programme appears in the base for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base states rural electricity access, a connection target or an off-grid programme for the country.

The only rural infrastructure documented is observational and not yet installed: [eleven hydrometeorological stations sited across three southern regions](2026-01-08-inm-gb-par-terceira-missao-terreno-sul-relatorio), reported station by station in a third field mission.

summary: The [2026 budget](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026) funds a financial system, a data centre, communications and an enterprise system; none is yet in service.
developments:
The [budget line](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026) is the first identified public money for government systems the base holds, covering the financial management system, a data centre, communications and an enterprise system.

Against it, delivery has been slow where it is measurable: the [fibre backbone tender was relaunched after two cancelled rounds](2026-03-17-worldbank-wardip-p176932-procurement-plan-guinea-bissau) and a master's assessment finds [electronic governance thin and blocked by weak infrastructure and the absence of a legal framework](2026-04-15-guinebissau-ipg-governacao-electronica-desafios-desenvolvimento).

summary: Justice-sector staff [completed a digital literacy course](2026-07-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-apr-jun-2026-digital-skills-justice) and [terms of reference were issued](2026-05-01-smartafrica-sada-wardip-sop1-tor-academic-partners) to train policymakers.
developments:
Capacity is being added course by course, and all of it is donor-financed. Justice-sector staff [completed a digital literacy course with an offline platform installed](2026-07-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-apr-jun-2026-digital-skills-justice), and [data protection capacity training ran in late 2025](2026-02-01-guinebissau-undp-newsletter-oct-dec-2025).

The largest planned intervention is regional: [terms of reference issued in May 2026 to recruit academic partners delivering training for policymakers across Guinea-Bissau and three peer states](2026-05-01-smartafrica-sada-wardip-sop1-tor-academic-partners). Tax officials were separately [trained on the revenue platform ahead of its September 2025 value added tax rollout](2025-08-06-guinebissau-ang-dgci-capacitacao-iva-kontaktu).

summary: [Decree 27/2025](2025-10-31-gnb-decreto-27-2025-regulamento-nacional-interoperabilidade) sets the rules and [consultants delivered the platform design](2025-11-15-wardip-gnb-publication-page-devemerge-interoperability-deliverable); nothing is recorded exchanging data through it.
developments:
The interoperability platform sits on the ledger as in development, and both of its preconditions arrived in the window: the [national interoperability regulation approved by decree in October 2025](2025-10-31-gnb-decreto-27-2025-regulamento-nacional-interoperabilidade) and the [delivered interoperability structure, platform and digitisation action plan](2025-11-15-wardip-gnb-publication-page-devemerge-interoperability-deliverable) in November.

What the base does not hold is any system connected to it. The [interoperability regulation for public and private digital services](2026-08-08-guineabissau-national-interoperability-framework) is enacted and in force, and no participant is named.

summary: The regional biometric card was [issued to more than 260 women traders at the Senegalese border](2026-03-20-ecowas-enbic-sao-domingos-262-women-traders) in March 2026.
developments:
The clearest documented use of the credential is cross-border trade: a [pilot handover at the Guinea-Bissau-Senegal border issued regional biometric cards to more than 260 women traders](2026-03-20-ecowas-enbic-sao-domingos-262-women-traders) in March 2026.

The direction of travel is regional: a [consultation opened in February 2026 on a roadmap from national identification systems to the regional card](2026-02-09-ecowas-roadmap-foundational-id-to-enbic-consultation). Domestically the identity number has not been linked to any other register on the record.

summary: A [track and trace mandate](2025-09-26-antares-vision-guinea-bissau-track-trace-mandate-digital-health) came into force in September 2025 and a [US$5m warehouse](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund) gives real-time medicine tracking.
developments:
The pharmaceutical chain is where health data exchange has actually been built: a [track and trace mandate centred on the regulator's drug catalogue came into force on 19 September 2025](2025-09-26-antares-vision-guinea-bissau-track-trace-mandate-digital-health), and a [US$5m solar-powered warehouse gives the central procurement body real-time medicine tracking](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund).

The national health platform is being extended separately, with a [grant placing Guinea-Bissau among seven countries receiving climate and health data tools](2025-12-22-dhis2-global-fund-climate-health-catalytic-guinea-bissau), and [health data use for decisions named among seven priorities in the 2026-2027 cooperation plan](2026-04-29-who-afro-guinea-bissau-biennial-workplan-2026-2027).

summary: A financed programme is [building a nationwide school, teacher and student database](2026-02-19-gnb-gpe-better-data-education-prieqt).
developments:
The system it replaces produced its [last published yearbook for 2014/15](2025-10-20-fec-peside-sige-2-0-estatisticas-educacao-guine-bissau), with statistics training beginning across four regions in October 2025.

The [financed programme confirmed in February 2026 is building a nationwide school, teacher and student database](2026-02-19-gnb-gpe-better-data-education-prieqt) with training on the education planning system and mobile data collection. Separately a [monitoring dashboard replaced paper inspection forms, with 78 inspectors covering 568 schools](2026-06-12-gnb-gems-school-monitoring-worldbank).

summary: No social protection register or management system is described for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base names a Guinean social registry, beneficiary database or social protection management system.

The delivery mechanisms that exist run through payroll rather than a register: the blockchain wage bill and pensions platform the ledger carries, and the [payment institution licensing that made electronic money possible at all](2025-09-15-bceao-liste-etablissements-paiement-agrees-umoa).

summary: The [eighteenth identity card production centre](2026-06-08-gnb-ang-bolama-centro-producao-bilhete-identidade) opened in June 2026, and a [third enrolment centre](2026-03-09-semlex-inauguration-centre-enrolement-sao-domingos) in February.
developments:
Coverage is being built through physical estate rather than through a national campaign: a [third regional enrolment centre opened in February 2026](2026-03-09-semlex-inauguration-centre-enrolement-sao-domingos) and the [eighteenth production centre nationwide in June](2026-06-08-gnb-ang-bolama-centro-producao-bilhete-identidade).

No enrolment total is published against those centres. The nearest population figure the base holds for an identity-adjacent register is the [electoral roll of 966,152](2025-08-15-ang-gtape-966152-eleitores-caderno-eleitoral).

summary: Production runs on a [contractor's network](2026-03-09-semlex-inauguration-centre-enrolement-sao-domingos); no statute or state operator is on the record.
developments:
The identity card production and enrolment network is a contractor's, and the base holds no Guinean statute governing it and no state body named as its operator.

What the state does is open centres: [eighteen production centres nationwide by June 2026](2026-06-08-gnb-ang-bolama-centro-producao-bilhete-identidade). The regional card scheme is likewise external, with a [roadmap consultation opened in February 2026](2026-02-09-ecowas-roadmap-foundational-id-to-enbic-consultation).

summary: No verification service exists; the identity card is presented rather than queried.
developments:
Nothing in the base records a service that checks a Guinean identity number against the register.

The interoperability rules that would allow one are new — the [national interoperability regulation approved by decree in October 2025](2025-10-31-gnb-decreto-27-2025-regulamento-nacional-interoperabilidade) and the [delivered platform design](2025-11-15-wardip-gnb-publication-page-devemerge-interoperability-deliverable) — and no participant system is named against either.

summary: Birth registration now happens at [school enrolment](2025-08-05-ang-acordo-justica-educacao-registo-nascimento-matricula) and in [health services](2025-09-04-gnb-unicef-nascer-com-identidade-registo-nascimento-saude), which registered 20,000 children in nine months.
developments:
Two service points were added to the register in the window. The justice and education ministries [agreed in August 2025 to issue birth registration at the moment of school enrolment](2025-08-05-ang-acordo-justica-educacao-registo-nascimento-matricula), and [more than 20,000 children were registered through health services in the nine months to June 2025](2025-09-04-gnb-unicef-nascer-com-identidade-registo-nascimento-saude).

A [third mobile justice caravan using the digital registration system launched in June 2026](2026-06-01-gnb-ang-candonga-di-justica-2026-sirec-registo-movel) for children's birth registration. Registration is not an identifier: no number is assigned at birth on the record.

summary: Registration reaches new service points but no link from the register to the identity card is described.
developments:
The register is being pushed outward — to [school enrolment](2025-08-05-ang-acordo-justica-educacao-registo-nascimento-matricula), to [health services](2025-09-04-gnb-unicef-nascer-com-identidade-registo-nascimento-saude) and to [mobile caravans](2026-06-01-gnb-ang-candonga-di-justica-2026-sirec-registo-movel) — and the base describes no connection between it and the identity card production network.

The first fully digital registry office opened in the window, at [Santa Luzia](2026-04-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-05-jan-mar-2026), which is a digitisation of the office rather than a link to another system.

summary: The regional card was [used for cross-border trade by more than 260 women](2026-03-20-ecowas-enbic-sao-domingos-262-women-traders); no domestic system consumes the identity.
developments:
The one recorded downstream use is regional rather than domestic: [more than 260 women traders received regional biometric cards at the Senegalese border](2026-03-20-ecowas-enbic-sao-domingos-262-women-traders) in a pilot handover.

Inside the country the registers run on their own identifiers — the [tax identification number issued solely through the payment platform](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu) and the electoral roll — and none is recorded checking against the identity register.

summary: The [central bank register](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau) carries six banks, one payment institution and one electronic money issuer as at June 2026.
developments:
Payment governance is the monetary union's rather than the country's. The [first licensed payment institution in Guinea-Bissau appeared on the union register in September 2025](2025-09-15-bceao-liste-etablissements-paiement-agrees-umoa), and the [June 2026 register lists six banks, one payment institution and one electronic money issuer](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau).

No domestic payments regulator, national switch governance or oversight publication appears in the base.

summary: The blockchain wage bill and pensions platform remains the only government-to-person rail described.
developments:
Nothing in this batch adds to the government-to-person picture beyond the wage bill and pensions platform the ledger already carries.

What the window does establish is that the rails around it are thin: [one licensed payment institution and one electronic money issuer in the whole country](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau) as at June 2026, and [only 22 per cent of women holding a bank or mobile money account](2026-04-02-guinebissau-world-bank-gender-data-landscape-2026).

summary: The payment platform became the [sole channel for the tax identification number](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu) and for [value added tax on customs clearance](2025-12-10-dgci-circular-iva-desalfandegamento-kontaktu).
developments:
Two orders in December 2025 made the simplified payment platform compulsory rather than optional: the revenue directorate [banned the older financial system and made the platform the sole channel for issuing the tax identification number](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu), and [mandated platform-only declaration and payment of value added tax for customs clearance, effective immediately](2025-12-10-dgci-circular-iva-desalfandegamento-kontaktu).

Staff were prepared for it: [tax officials in fiscal districts and regional offices were trained ahead of the September 2025 value added tax rollout](2025-08-06-guinebissau-ang-dgci-capacitacao-iva-kontaktu). The fund's [eleventh review names the platform and a taxpayer census among reform actions](2026-06-01-imf-cr-26-140-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review).

summary: Importers must [declare and pay value added tax through the platform](2025-12-10-dgci-circular-iva-desalfandegamento-kontaktu) to clear customs, from December 2025.
developments:
The [circular of December 2025](2025-12-10-dgci-circular-iva-desalfandegamento-kontaktu) makes business-to-government payment electronic by compulsion: importers declare the tax they have borne on the customs declaration and pay exclusively through the platform.

The cross-border trade layer is being built regionally: a [Bissau workshop presented the union's paperless customs directive and a planned trade-document exchange platform](2026-04-28-ang-uemoa-bissau-workshop-plataforma-eletronica-documentos-comerciais) in April 2026.

summary: The country gained its [first licensed payment institution](2025-09-15-bceao-liste-etablissements-paiement-agrees-umoa) in September 2025.
developments:
Retail electronic payment capacity is new and small: the [first payment institution licensed under the monetary union appeared on the register in September 2025](2025-09-15-bceao-liste-etablissements-paiement-agrees-umoa), and by [June 2026 the country had one payment institution and one electronic money issuer](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau).

Person-to-government payment is the mature side, through the [simplified tax and contribution payment platform](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu) the revenue directorate has made compulsory.

summary: Cross-border capability is the monetary union's; no national instrument is held.
developments:
Guinea-Bissau's payment rails are union rails, and the base holds no national cross-border instrument. The [union register of authorised establishments](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau) is the operative list.

What is being built across borders is documents rather than money: the [paperless customs directive and trade-document platform presented at Bissau in April 2026](2026-04-28-ang-uemoa-bissau-workshop-plataforma-eletronica-documentos-comerciais).

summary: No payment consumer protection instrument appears in the base for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base records a complaints route, a redress rule or a disclosure requirement for Guinean payment users.

Authorisation is the only protection documented, and it is the union's: [six banks, one payment institution and one electronic money issuer on the register](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau) as at June 2026.

summary: The [fourth census launched field enumeration](2026-06-01-unfpa-guinea-bissau-rgph4-census-field-launch) in June 2026, the first fully digital count since 2009.
developments:
The institute [opened recruitment for about 5,000 census staff](2025-09-02-ang-ine-gb-plataforma-recrutamento-rgph4) in September 2025 and [launched field enumeration in June 2026](2026-06-01-unfpa-guinea-bissau-rgph4-census-field-launch), the country's first fully digital census since 2009.

The continuous register beside it is the civil register, whose [first fully digital office opened at Santa Luzia](2026-04-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-05-jan-mar-2026). No population register linking the two is described.

summary: No addressing system, postcode scheme or street register appears in the base for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base records a Guinean address register, a national addressing programme or a postcode scheme.

The geographic reference work that is happening is agricultural and meteorological: [eleven hydrometeorological stations sited across three southern regions](2026-01-08-inm-gb-par-terceira-missao-terreno-sul-relatorio) and satellite growing-season monitoring produced by international agencies.

summary: [743 new companies were registered in 2025](2026-02-02-ang-cfe-743-novas-empresas-2025), up 24 per cent, with formation taking about five hours.
developments:
The registry's own director general gives the figures: [743 new companies in 2025 against 598 in 2024, with company formation now taking about five hours](2026-02-02-ang-cfe-743-novas-empresas-2025).

It is the one Guinean register in the base publishing a throughput series and a service-time claim. The tax side hardened alongside it, with the [tax identification number issued solely through the payment platform from December 2025](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu).

summary: No social registry is described; payment runs through the [wage bill and pensions platform](2024-10-02-imf-country-focus-guinea-bissau-blockchain-wage-bill) rather than a beneficiary register.
developments:
Nothing in the base names a Guinean social registry or beneficiary database.

What exists is a payment rail on the ledger — the blockchain wage bill and pensions platform — and a financial system too thin to carry transfers widely: [one payment institution and one electronic money issuer nationally](2026-06-29-cb-umoa-liste-etablissements-agrees-guinee-bissau), and [22 per cent of women holding an account](2026-04-02-guinebissau-world-bank-gender-data-landscape-2026).

summary: The tax identification number is [issued solely through the payment platform](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu) from December 2025, with a [taxpayer census as a reform action](2026-06-01-imf-cr-26-140-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review).
developments:
The revenue directorate's [order of December 2025 bans the older financial management system and makes the payment platform the sole channel for producing and issuing the tax identification number](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu).

The register behind it is to be rebuilt: the fund's [eleventh review confirms the revenue administration platform and a taxpayer census among the reform actions](2026-06-01-imf-cr-26-140-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review). No taxpayer count is published.

summary: Eight states [approved a draft directive harmonising land registration](2026-06-26-uemoa-directive-immatriculation-propriete-fonciere) in June 2026; no domestic register is described.
developments:
The base holds no account of a Guinean land register, cadastre or titling system.

The movement is regional and prospective: eight member states [approved a draft directive harmonising land registration and titling rules across the union](2026-06-26-uemoa-directive-immatriculation-propriete-fonciere) in June 2026. No domestic transposition or register is recorded.

summary: A [track and trace mandate](2025-09-26-antares-vision-guinea-bissau-track-trace-mandate-digital-health) and a [US$5m tracked warehouse](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund) put the medicine chain on a system.
developments:
The health system's clearest digital asset is its supply chain: a [pharmaceutical track and trace mandate centred on the regulator's drug catalogue came into force in September 2025](2025-09-26-antares-vision-guinea-bissau-track-trace-mandate-digital-health), and a [US$5m solar-powered warehouse gives real-time medicine tracking](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund).

The information platform is being extended with a [grant for climate and health data tools](2025-12-22-dhis2-global-fund-climate-health-catalytic-guinea-bissau), and [health data use for decisions is named among seven priorities in the 2026-2027 cooperation plan](2026-04-29-who-afro-guinea-bissau-biennial-workplan-2026-2027).

summary: A [monitoring dashboard replaced paper inspections](2026-06-12-gnb-gems-school-monitoring-worldbank), 78 inspectors covering 568 schools.
developments:
The [dashboard](2026-06-12-gnb-gems-school-monitoring-worldbank) is the base's clearest working education system: 78 inspectors covering 568 schools, replacing paper inspection forms.

The statistical side is further behind — the [last published yearbook dates to 2014/15](2025-10-20-fec-peside-sige-2-0-estatisticas-educacao-guine-bissau) — and a [financed programme is building a nationwide school, teacher and student database](2026-02-19-gnb-gpe-better-data-education-prieqt) to fix it. An [assessment with 34 stakeholders in November 2025](2026-03-01-gpe-technology-for-education-initiative-progress-report-2025) rated the sector's digital maturity.

summary: No social protection management system is described for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base names a Guinean social protection management information system, case management tool or beneficiary tracking platform.

The programme layer that would use one is documented only at project level, through the [peacebuilding fund's June 2025 progress report covering ten projects from electoral law to digital-media training](2025-08-03-guinebissau-pbf-00119912-project-progress-report-june-2025).

summary: Justice-sector staff [completed a digital literacy course with an offline platform installed](2026-07-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-apr-jun-2026-digital-skills-justice).
developments:
The criminal information system sits on the ledger as implemented. What moved in the window is the people around it: justice-sector staff [completed a digital literacy course and an offline learning platform was installed](2026-07-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-apr-jun-2026-digital-skills-justice).

The justice ministry is also the register's operator, running the [mobile caravans that carry digital birth registration into communities](2026-06-01-gnb-ang-candonga-di-justica-2026-sirec-registo-movel).

summary: The payment platform is now [compulsory for the tax identification number](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu) and [for value added tax on imports](2025-12-10-dgci-circular-iva-desalfandegamento-kontaktu).
developments:
The platform has moved from a channel to the channel: [sole issuer of the tax identification number from December 2025](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu), with the older financial management system banned for the purpose, and [exclusive route for declaring and paying import value added tax](2025-12-10-dgci-circular-iva-desalfandegamento-kontaktu).

It is doing so under external condition: the fund's [eleventh review names the revenue administration platform and a taxpayer census as reform actions](2026-06-01-imf-cr-26-140-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review), with [US$1.6m to US$1.7m disbursed on completion](2026-06-12-imf-pr-26-204-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review).

summary: Customs runs on the international customs platform; a [regional trade-document platform](2026-04-28-ang-uemoa-bissau-workshop-plataforma-eletronica-documentos-comerciais) was presented at Bissau in April 2026.
developments:
The customs management system sits on the ledger as implemented. Around it, [importers must now declare and pay value added tax through the revenue platform to clear customs](2025-12-10-dgci-circular-iva-desalfandegamento-kontaktu), which ties the two systems together at the point of clearance.

The regional layer is prospective: a [Bissau workshop presented the union's paperless customs directive and a planned electronic trade-document exchange platform](2026-04-28-ang-uemoa-bissau-workshop-plataforma-eletronica-documentos-comerciais) in April 2026.

summary: No land management system is described; the [regional directive](2026-06-26-uemoa-directive-immatriculation-propriete-fonciere) is the only instrument on the record.
developments:
The base holds nothing on Guinean land administration systems, cadastral mapping or titling workflows.

The only relevant document is regional and at draft stage: the [directive harmonising land registration and titling rules approved by eight member states in June 2026](2026-06-26-uemoa-directive-immatriculation-propriete-fonciere).

summary: A [one-stop digitalised transport counter opened at Gabu](2026-03-19-ang-gabu-centro-servicos-integrados-transportes), the first outside the capital.
developments:
Electronic government is assessed as thin by the one academic study the base holds: [blocked by weak infrastructure and the absence of a legal framework](2026-04-15-guinebissau-ipg-governacao-electronica-desafios-desenvolvimento).

Against that, delivery has started: a [one-stop digitalised transport licensing counter opened at Gabu in March 2026, the first outside Bissau](2026-03-19-ang-gabu-centro-servicos-integrados-transportes), and the [digitisation action plan for the main public services was delivered in November 2025](2025-11-15-wardip-gnb-publication-page-devemerge-interoperability-deliverable). The [national programme launched in August 2026 carries electronic government among its four strands](2026-08-01-gnb-ang-wardip-lancamento-nacional-digitalizacao).

summary: The first integrated service counter outside the capital [opened at Gabu](2026-03-19-ang-gabu-centro-servicos-integrados-transportes) in March 2026.
developments:
The structural constraint is stated plainly by a conference that closed in October 2025: [three decades of democracy with no local elections yet held](2025-10-22-imvf-conferencia-internacional-descentralizacao-guine-bissau), and recommendations for training local technical staff and managers.

What has arrived is central service delivery pushed outward: a [one-stop digitalised transport licensing counter at Gabu](2026-03-19-ang-gabu-centro-servicos-integrados-transportes), the [first fully digital civil registry office at Santa Luzia](2026-04-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-05-jan-mar-2026), and [eighteen identity card production centres nationwide](2026-06-08-gnb-ang-bolama-centro-producao-bilhete-identidade).

summary: No municipal record system is described; [no local elections have been held in three decades](2025-10-22-imvf-conferencia-internacional-descentralizacao-guine-bissau).
developments:
Nothing in the base records a Guinean municipal register, local revenue system or council record platform.

The reason is structural rather than technical: a [decentralisation conference closed in October 2025 recording that no local elections have been held in three decades of democracy](2025-10-22-imvf-conferencia-internacional-descentralizacao-guine-bissau), and recommending the training of local technical staff and managers as a precondition.

summary: The medicine chain reaches facilities through a [tracked central warehouse](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund); no clinic-level system is described.
developments:
The [US$5m solar-powered warehouse commissioned in October 2025](2025-10-06-gnb-undp-smart-warehouse-in-a-box-global-fund) gives the central procurement body real-time medicine tracking, which is the supply side of rural health delivery.

No facility-level record system outside the capital is named in the base. The [track and trace mandate](2025-09-26-antares-vision-guinea-bissau-track-trace-mandate-digital-health) governs the product rather than the clinic.

summary: [78 inspectors covering 568 schools](2026-06-12-gnb-gems-school-monitoring-worldbank) report through a dashboard rather than on paper.
developments:
The [monitoring dashboard](2026-06-12-gnb-gems-school-monitoring-worldbank) is the base's only evidence of digital reach across Guinean schools, and it is inspection rather than teaching: 78 inspectors, 568 schools, replacing paper forms.

An [assessment with 34 stakeholders in November 2025](2026-03-01-gpe-technology-for-education-initiative-progress-report-2025) rated the sector's digital maturity, and [statistics training began across four regions](2025-10-20-fec-peside-sige-2-0-estatisticas-educacao-guine-bissau) in October 2025. No count of connected schools is published.

summary: [Santa Luzia became the first fully digital civil registry office](2026-04-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-05-jan-mar-2026) under the integrated register system.
developments:
The [office at Santa Luzia](2026-04-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-05-jan-mar-2026) is the country's first fully digital civil registry office, which makes it the base's clearest measure of how far digitisation has reached outside the capital: one office.

Registration itself travels instead: [mobile justice caravans carrying digital registration for children](2026-06-01-gnb-ang-candonga-di-justica-2026-sirec-registo-movel) and [registration at health services, more than 20,000 children in nine months](2025-09-04-gnb-unicef-nascer-com-identidade-registo-nascimento-saude).

summary: No station-level system is described; the [criminal information system](2023-03-09-pj-guine-bissau-inauguracao-siic-sistema-integrado-informacao-criminal) has no recorded deployment outside the capital.
developments:
Nothing in the base records digital records, connectivity or case management at Guinean police stations outside Bissau.

The country's police data commitments are external: [participation in the West African police information system, confirmed in September 2025](2025-09-12-interpol-president-guinea-bissau-declaration-of-intent) alongside the privileges and immunities agreement.

summary: No artificial intelligence is recorded inside Guinean government administration.
developments:
Nothing in the base names an artificial intelligence tool, pilot or procurement inside a Guinean ministry or agency.
