Where officials have engaged with the subject it has been abroad and at forum level: the [public works ministry joined an artificial-intelligence-in-infrastructure capacity forum under the Sino-Lusophone framework](2026-06-12-forum-macau-capacitacao-inteligencia-artificial-cooperacao-sino-lusofona) among more than 120 delegates in June 2026.

summary: A grant places Guinea-Bissau among [seven countries receiving climate and health data tools](2025-12-22-dhis2-global-fund-climate-health-catalytic-guinea-bissau) for the health platform.
developments:
The [grant confirmed in December 2025](2025-12-22-dhis2-global-fund-climate-health-catalytic-guinea-bissau) is the only instance in the base of analytic tooling being added to a Guinean sectoral system, and it is one of seven countries in a single programme rather than a national initiative.

No tool is recorded in use, and the platform's own priorities are set externally: [health data use for decisions named among seven priorities in the 2026-2027 cooperation plan](2026-04-29-who-afro-guinea-bissau-biennial-workplan-2026-2027).

summary: No Guinean artificial intelligence system, model or product is on the record.
developments:
Nothing in the base records an artificial intelligence system built in or for Guinea-Bissau.

The country's engagement is participatory: a [Bissau forum on artificial intelligence, ethics and disinformation](2025-11-11-nokunsi-djumbai-inteligencia-artificial-bissau) in November 2025, a [training session covering digital content, artificial intelligence ethics and online safety for 22 youth-network leaders](2025-08-06-guinebissau-unfpa-digital-training-youth-networks), and the [Macau capacity forum](2026-06-12-forum-macau-capacitacao-inteligencia-artificial-cooperacao-sino-lusofona).

summary: Ministers of Guinea-Bissau and The Gambia [pledged joint action on misinformation](2026-06-24-voicegambia-gambia-guinea-bissau-cooperation-misinformation-ai) as artificial intelligence accelerates it.
developments:
The response so far is cooperation and framework rather than rule: [ministers pledged joint action in June 2026 as artificial intelligence accelerates the spread of unverified information](2026-06-24-voicegambia-gambia-guinea-bissau-cooperation-misinformation-ai), and a [regional framework adopted the same month commits fifteen West African states to information-integrity laws for 2026-2036](2026-07-01-ang-quadro-politico-integridade-informacao-africa-ocidental-sahel).

The domestic instrument that exists names no technology: the [law against the dissemination of false information online](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais), passed by a transitional council that had [blocked four platforms nationwide six months earlier](2025-11-27-mfwa-guinea-bissau-military-takeover-media-suspension).

summary: No domestic technology production is recorded; equipment is [tendered and imported](2026-05-15-guinebissau-agefp-acordo-quadro-material-informatico).
developments:
Nothing in the base records Guinean production of hardware, software or digital services for sale.

What is documented is procurement: the [employment and vocational training agency tendered a framework agreement for computing equipment in May 2026](2026-05-15-guinebissau-agefp-acordo-quadro-material-informatico), and the identity card production network is a [contractor's estate](2026-03-09-semlex-inauguration-centre-enrolement-sao-domingos).

summary: An operator's digital centre [moved to a structured incubation and acceleration programme](2026-04-30-orange-bissau-odc-programa-incubacao-aceleracao-startups) in April 2026.
developments:
Hubs arrived in the window rather than before it. An [incubator opened in Bissau in September 2025 training 15 youth entrepreneurs chosen from 52 proposals](2025-09-25-guinebissau-ang-incubadora-inodevgb), and an [operator's digital centre moved from ad hoc training to a structured incubation and acceleration programme](2026-04-30-orange-bissau-odc-programa-incubacao-aceleracao-startups) in April 2026.

Both are small and both are externally funded; neither publishes a graduate or survival figure.

summary: A digital economy fund [selected its first cohort of 30 projects](2026-03-04-wardip-orik-capital-30-projetos-primeira-turma-empreendedorismo-digital) in March 2026.
developments:
The fund and the programme launched together: a [digital economy cluster and entrepreneurship fund opened in Bissau in October 2025](2025-10-31-innovalab-cluster-economia-digital-orik-capital-wardip), and [selected its first cohort of 30 digital entrepreneurship projects in March 2026](2026-03-04-wardip-orik-capital-30-projetos-primeira-turma-empreendedorismo-digital) under the regional digital programme.

No investment total, company count or survival figure is published. The [52 proposals to a single incubator in 2025](2025-09-25-guinebissau-ang-incubadora-inodevgb) is the base's only measure of demand.

summary: Justice-sector staff [completed a digital literacy course](2026-07-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-apr-jun-2026-digital-skills-justice) and an offline learning platform was installed.
developments:
Provision is course-by-course and donor-financed: justice-sector staff [completed a digital literacy course with an offline platform installed](2026-07-01-undp-guinea-bissau-newsletter-apr-jun-2026-digital-skills-justice), [data protection capacity training ran in late 2025 with a civic input application piloted](2026-02-01-guinebissau-undp-newsletter-oct-dec-2025), and [tax officials were trained on the revenue platform](2025-08-06-guinebissau-ang-dgci-capacitacao-iva-kontaktu) ahead of the value added tax rollout.

The policy that would organise it is new: the [National Digital Skills Policy decree approved by the Council of Ministers in May 2026](2026-05-19-guine-bissau-comunicado-conselho-ministros-politica-nacional-competencias-digitais).

summary: No secondary computing curriculum is described; the [education programme](2026-02-19-gnb-gpe-better-data-education-prieqt) is about data rather than teaching.
developments:
Nothing in the base states whether Guinean secondary schools teach computing, or to how many pupils.

The education technology work that is documented is administrative: a [nationwide school, teacher and student database](2026-02-19-gnb-gpe-better-data-education-prieqt) and a [maturity assessment with 34 stakeholders](2026-03-01-gpe-technology-for-education-initiative-progress-report-2025) in November 2025. The [digital skills policy approved in May 2026](2026-05-19-guine-bissau-comunicado-conselho-ministros-politica-nacional-competencias-digitais) is the instrument that would set a curriculum, and its text is not held.

summary: A [Portuguese polytechnic opened 2025/26 places](2025-12-03-ipv-edital-protocolo-guine-bissau-estudantes-internacionais-2025-2026) for Guinean students in informatics and telecommunications.
developments:
Domestic provision is thin and physical: a [regional university reported 90 per cent readiness with 60 computers en route for the 2025/26 intake](2025-08-11-guinebissau-ang-universidade-reino-bassarel-canchungo), and the [vocational training agency tendered a computing equipment framework in May 2026](2026-05-15-guinebissau-agefp-acordo-quadro-material-informatico).

Degree-level provision is partly abroad: a [Portuguese polytechnic opened 2025/26 places for Guinean students in informatics and telecommunications under a collaboration protocol](2025-12-03-ipv-edital-protocolo-guine-bissau-estudantes-internacionais-2025-2026).

summary: No graduate count or destination series exists for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base counts Guinean technology graduates, or where they go.

The cohorts that are counted are small and programme-shaped: [15 entrepreneurs from 52 proposals at one incubator](2025-09-25-guinebissau-ang-incubadora-inodevgb), [30 projects in a fund's first cohort](2026-03-04-wardip-orik-capital-30-projetos-primeira-turma-empreendedorismo-digital), [22 youth-network leaders trained in digital content and online safety](2025-08-06-guinebissau-unfpa-digital-training-youth-networks) and [50 women completing a digital security and financial literacy trainer course](2026-07-03-guinebissau-ang-impact-hub-competencias-digitais-50-mulheres).

summary: A [master's dissertation](2026-04-15-guinebissau-ipg-governacao-electronica-desafios-desenvolvimento) finds electronic governance blocked by weak infrastructure and no legal framework.
developments:
Two pieces of research bearing on Guinean digital policy appeared in the window, and neither was produced by a Guinean institution. A [master's dissertation at a Portuguese polytechnic finds electronic governance thin, blocked by weak infrastructure and the absence of a legal framework](2026-04-15-guinebissau-ipg-governacao-electronica-desafios-desenvolvimento), and a [preprint maps the online networks of around 445,000 followers behind political mobilisation since 2013](2025-09-10-guinebissau-scielo-preprint-ciberativismo-resistencia).

The domestic research network the ledger carries remains planned.

summary: A [youth feedback platform launched on text message and messaging apps](2025-10-01-guinebissau-ang-ureport-lancamento-participacao-juvenil) in October 2025.
developments:
The [platform launched on 1 October 2025](2025-10-01-guinebissau-ang-ureport-lancamento-participacao-juvenil) with an international agency and a mobile operator is the base's only citizen feedback channel for Guinea-Bissau, and it is youth-specific.

A second was piloted rather than launched: a [civic input application](2026-02-01-guinebissau-undp-newsletter-oct-dec-2025) in late 2025. No response or resolution figure is published for either.

summary: A [youth dialogue closed with policy recommendations](2025-10-01-guinebissau-un-dialogo-com-a-juventude) weeks before [platforms were blocked nationwide](2025-11-27-mfwa-guinea-bissau-military-takeover-media-suspension).
developments:
Structured participation was running: a [youth leadership dialogue closed with policy recommendations](2025-10-01-guinebissau-un-dialogo-com-a-juventude) in October 2025, and the [peacebuilding fund's progress report covers ten projects from electoral law to digital-media training](2025-08-03-guinebissau-pbf-00119912-project-progress-report-june-2025).

The channel narrowed a month later: [radio shutdowns and a nationwide block on four major platforms](2025-11-27-mfwa-guinea-bissau-military-takeover-media-suspension) after the November 2025 takeover, followed by a [law against false online information in May 2026](2026-05-21-ang-cnt-aprova-lei-contra-falsas-informacoes-redes-sociais).

progress: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
summary: [Women hold 49 per cent of the legal rights men hold and 22 per cent have an account](2026-04-02-guinebissau-world-bank-gender-data-landscape-2026).
developments:
The [gender data landscape published in April 2026](2026-04-02-guinebissau-world-bank-gender-data-landscape-2026) is the first sex-disaggregated evidence the base holds for Guinea-Bissau: women hold 49 per cent of the legal rights men hold, and only 22 per cent have a bank or mobile money account.

The training response is small and counted: [50 women completed a seven-day digital security and financial literacy trainer course](2026-07-03-guinebissau-ang-impact-hub-competencias-digitais-50-mulheres) in July 2026, and [more than 260 women traders received regional biometric cards at the border](2026-03-20-ecowas-enbic-sao-domingos-262-women-traders) in March.

summary: An agency [delivered mobility and computing equipment to the national disability federation](2026-02-12-guinebissau-unfpa-entrega-equipamentos-fadpd) for data advocacy.
developments:
The [delivery of February 2026](2026-02-12-guinebissau-unfpa-entrega-equipamentos-fadpd) — wheelchairs, crutches and a computing kit to the national disability federation for data advocacy — is the only disability-related digital record the base holds for Guinea-Bissau.

No disability statute, accessibility standard or disability-disaggregated access figure appears anywhere in the file.

summary: [32 refugees and 37 returnees](2026-05-31-guinebissau-unhcr-operational-data-portal-country-page) recorded at 31 May 2026.
developments:
The [agency's operational data](2026-05-31-guinebissau-unhcr-operational-data-portal-country-page) records 32 refugees and 37 returnees for Guinea-Bissau at 31 May 2026.

The population is small enough that no dedicated registration, documentation or service system is described for it, and none appears in the base.

summary: A [2026-2031 universal access fund plan](2026-05-01-wardip-plano-estrategico-fundo-acesso-servicos-universais-2026-2031) sets targets for closing the coverage gap.
developments:
The instrument was found wanting first: a [legal review recommended restructuring the universal access fund](2025-10-30-guinebissau-wardip-revisao-quadro-legal-acesso-servico-universal) in October 2025.

The [2026-2031 strategic and financing plan](2026-05-01-wardip-plano-estrategico-fundo-acesso-servicos-universais-2026-2031) followed, and the network it would fund is still at tender: the [fibre backbone relaunched in March 2026 after two cancelled rounds](2026-03-17-wardip-concurso-internacional-rede-nacional-fibra-optica). Regionally, [five states evaluated bids for a second submarine cable in Abuja](2026-07-06-ecowas-wardip-submarine-cable-capacity-evaluation-committee) in July 2026.

summary: No statistics development strategy is held; the [2007 framework law](2007-09-10-ine-guine-bissau-lei-6-2007-sistema-estatistico-nacional) and the census are the system's whole record.
developments:
The base holds no Guinean national strategy for the development of statistics.

What it holds is the statutory frame and the operation: the 2007 framework law on the ledger, and the [fourth census launched into field enumeration in June 2026](2026-06-01-unfpa-guinea-bissau-rgph4-census-field-launch) after [recruitment opened for about 5,000 staff](2025-09-02-ang-ine-gb-plataforma-recrutamento-rgph4).

summary: [Civil registry professionals were trained in data skills](2025-08-08-unfpa-guinea-bissau-civil-registry-statistics-training) in August 2025.
developments:
The [training of August 2025](2025-08-08-unfpa-guinea-bissau-civil-registry-statistics-training) is the base's only evidence of statistical capacity being built inside the register that produces vital statistics.

The administrative streams that would feed a compilation are themselves being rebuilt — the [education database](2026-02-19-gnb-gpe-better-data-education-prieqt), the [school inspection dashboard](2026-06-12-gnb-gems-school-monitoring-worldbank) and the [tax platform](2025-12-03-dgci-instrucao-servico-25-2025-nif-kontaktu) — and none is recorded reaching the statistics institute.

summary: No open data portal or dataset release is recorded; the [national summary data page](2024-07-08-imf-pr24262-guinea-bissau-implements-egdds-national-summary-data-page) is the only routine publication.
developments:
The base holds no Guinean open data portal, licence or dataset catalogue.

Routine publication is limited to two instruments the ledger already carries: the fund's national summary data page, and the [state budget volume published with the 2026 budget](2025-12-01-mef-guine-bissau-oge-2026). The access to information bill that would create a right of access remains in development.

summary: The [2025 cereal harvest came in 18 per cent above average](2026-02-06-fao-giews-country-brief-guinea-bissau), with satellite data flagging localised dry spells.
developments:
Two international agencies produce the country's satellite agriculture monitoring. A [rainy-season bulletin published rainfall, vegetation index and forecast data through August 2025](2025-08-01-wfp-guine-bissau-bulletin-suivi-saison-pluvieuse-aout-2025), and a [country brief of February 2026 puts the 2025 cereal harvest 18 per cent above average with satellite data flagging localised dry-spell shortfalls](2026-02-06-fao-giews-country-brief-guinea-bissau).

No Guinean agency is recorded operating an imagery capability of its own.

summary: The meteorological institute [operationalised the common alerting protocol](2026-05-07-inm-gb-operacionalizacao-do-cap-sistemas-de-alerta), surfacing national alerts on search and maps.
developments:
The [operationalisation of May 2026](2026-05-07-inm-gb-operacionalizacao-do-cap-sistemas-de-alerta) puts Guinea-Bissau's weather alerts into general search and mapping services, which is the first time the institute's output reaches the public through a standard channel.

The observing network beneath it is still being sited: a [third field mission reported station-by-station findings for eleven hydrometeorological stations across three southern regions](2026-01-08-inm-gb-par-terceira-missao-terreno-sul-relatorio).

summary: No United States digital engagement is recorded for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base names a United States agency, development finance instrument or cloud company in connection with Guinean digital infrastructure.

The financing relationships that do exist are multilateral: the [fund's extended credit facility](2026-06-12-imf-pr-26-204-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review) and the [US$60m regional digital programme launched in August 2026](2026-08-01-gnb-ang-wardip-lancamento-nacional-digitalizacao).

summary: The public works ministry [joined an artificial intelligence capacity forum](2026-06-12-forum-macau-capacitacao-inteligencia-artificial-cooperacao-sino-lusofona) under the Sino-Lusophone framework.
developments:
The [forum of June 2026](2026-06-12-forum-macau-capacitacao-inteligencia-artificial-cooperacao-sino-lusofona) on artificial intelligence in infrastructure, convened under the Sino-Lusophone cooperation framework among more than 120 delegates, is the base's only record of Chinese digital engagement with Guinea-Bissau.

No instrument, financing or system follows from it, and no Chinese vendor appears anywhere else in the unit's file.

summary: European funding runs through programmes rather than instruments — the [justice caravans](2026-06-01-gnb-ang-candonga-di-justica-2026-sirec-registo-movel) are one.
developments:
No European Union memorandum or country digital programme appears in the base for Guinea-Bissau. What appears is co-financing of specific operations: the [third mobile justice caravan launched jointly with the development programme in June 2026](2026-06-01-gnb-ang-candonga-di-justica-2026-sirec-registo-movel), using the digital registration system for children's birth registration.

European involvement is otherwise institutional and educational: a [Portuguese polytechnic opening places for Guinean students in informatics and telecommunications](2025-12-03-ipv-edital-protocolo-guine-bissau-estudantes-internacionais-2025-2026).

summary: No Gulf state digital engagement is recorded for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base names a Gulf state, sovereign fund or operator in connection with Guinean digital infrastructure, financing or skills.

The country's external digital financing is multilateral and regional: the [US$60m programme launched in August 2026](2026-08-01-gnb-ang-wardip-lancamento-nacional-digitalizacao) and the [fund's credit facility reviews](2026-06-12-imf-pr-26-204-guinea-bissau-eleventh-ecf-review).

summary: No Indian digital engagement is recorded for Guinea-Bissau.
developments:
Nothing in the base names an Indian agency, credit line, training programme or system in connection with Guinea-Bissau's digital estate.

Where the country's officials have travelled for technology capacity building it has been to the [Sino-Lusophone forum in Macau](2026-06-12-forum-macau-capacitacao-inteligencia-artificial-cooperacao-sino-lusofona) rather than to an Indian programme.
